record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Characterize the Banach spaces that admit an equivalent strictly convex norm.

evidence.quote:
(Q.18) Characterize those Banach spaces which have an equivalent strictly convex
norm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A norm $\|\cdot\|$ on a real Banach space $X$ is called strictly convex (or rotund) if for all $x,y \in X$ with $\|x\|=\|y\|=1$ and $x\neq y$, one has $\left\|\tfrac{x+y}{2}\right\| < 1$; equivalently, the unit sphere of $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ contains no nontrivial line segment. Two norms $\|\cdot\|_1$ and $\|\cdot\|_2$ on $X$ are equivalent if there exist constants $0 < c \le C < \infty$ such that $c\|x\|_1 \le \|x\|_2 \le C\|x\|_1$ for every $x \in X$. A Banach space $(X,\|\cdot\|)$ is said to admit an equivalent strictly convex norm if there exists a strictly convex norm on $X$ equivalent to $\|\cdot\|$.

Provide an intrinsic characterization (for example, of topological, structural, or set-theoretic nature) of the class of Banach spaces $X$ that admit an equivalent strictly convex norm.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a general intrinsic characterization of Banach spaces admitting an equivalent strictly convex norm remains open. Partial results are known: every separable Banach space admits such a renorming (Clarkson/Day), while Haydon constructed scattered compacta $K$ such that $C(K)$ fails to be strictly convex renormable. Topological characterizations in special settings (e.g., for $C(K)^*$ over scattered $K$) have been obtained by Smith, Orihuela, Troyanski and others, but no general checkable criterion is known, and recent work (e.g., 2022–2024 arXiv papers on strictly convex renormings and the diameter-2 property) continues to investigate the question.

status_evidence.title: Strictly convex norms and topology
status_evidence.snippet: We give a topological characterization of those Banach spaces which admit an equivalent strictly convex norm... and an internal characterization of scattered compact spaces K for which C(K)* admits an equivalent strictly convex dual norm.
status_evidence.claim: Topological characterizations exist in special cases, but no general intrinsic characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Strictly convex renormings and the diameter 2 property
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies coexistence of strictly convex renormability with other geometric properties.
status_evidence.claim: The strict convex renorming problem continues to be actively studied.
